messages.subject: [time series] All pit=0 with lognormal surv
parts:
Hi,

In the attached code, I simulate a time series according to a RW1, take the exponential to switch to a lognormal distribution, add censoring and model using inla.surv() and lognormal.surv. All PIT values are equal to 0.

What am I doing wrong?

Thank you in advance and thank you for your availability and expertise.
Regards
Dominique

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] [time series] All pit=0 with lognormal surv
parts:
Pit is not computed for censored data, or survival models.  There can be information stored allowing you to compute it yourself ( depending on how you define pit for censored data).  But I have to check ….

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] [time series] All pit=0 with lognormal surv
parts:
r <- inla(Y ~ 1 + x,
data = list(Y=Y, x=x),
family = "exponentialsurv",
verbose = TRUE,
control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=1, prec=1))

## add this
## then you'll get mean and stdev of the linear predictor of y_i given y_{-i}
## and you can work
## it out from this one (assuming its Normal)
rr=inla.group.cv(r)
with(rr, cbind(mean, sd))
